items.headline: High-speed train crash kills at least 68 people in Spain
items.blurb: The crash, between a moving train and another that was stopped further up the track, was caused by an "inexplicable" error, the transport minister said.
items.text: A high-speed train crash has killed at least 68 people and injured dozens more in central Spain. It occurred when a train travelling from Madrid to Seville barrelled into another train - which was stationary on the tracks - on Wednesday morning. The force saw several carriages fall down an embankment. The transport minister said a computer failure followed by human error caused the crash, which is one of the worst in Europe's modern history, and Spain's deadliest train disaster in 13 years. Survivors described harrowing scenes of passengers being thrown into the air, trapped in the wreckage and smashing windows to get out. The crash happened just after 09:00 (08:00 GMT) around 140km (87 miles) south of Madrid, between the municipalities of Mora and Orgaz. The stationary train, run by private rail operator Iryo, had 147 passengers on board, and had stopped on the tracks because of a computer failure, Spain's Transport Minister Óscar Puente said. items.text: Warnings of escalating clampdown on press freedom come after Cairo court convicts Attalah of managing an unlicensed website Lina Attalah, a prominent Egyptian journalist and the editor-in-chief of the news outlet Mada Masr, has been released from detention by Egypt’s authorities and had her website ordered to be shut down by a court amid an intensifying crackdown on independent media in the country. Attalah was taken briefly into custody after a Cairo court convicted her of managing an unlicensed website, prompting fresh international concerns over press freedom in Egypt. According to Mada Masr, Attalah was released after the news outlet had paid a fine of 3m Egyptian pounds ($53,500; £40,100), prompting statements of support from global human rights groups. “Lina Attalah was released after we paid the said fine,” said her lawyer Hassan al-Azhari. “In the process, we discovered that she had been sentenced in absentia in 2024 to a year in prison, as well as a fine of 20,000 Egyptian pounds,” he told AFP. items.headline: Bloodied, dazed and angry - how passengers' rail journey turned to disaster in Spain
items.blurb: Survivors of the train crash in Spain have spoken of their shock, panic and anger at the accident in Toledo province on Wednesday.
items.text: It was approaching 08:30 (07:30 GMT) on a normal Wednesday. Two high-speed trains were travelling south from the Spanish capital, Madrid, to Seville. One, run by state-owned operator Renfe had 397 passengers on board. Ahead of it on the same line was a train of Iryo private operator with 147 passengers. A reported issue with the automatic signalling system - a computer failure - had forced all trains to halt on the affected stretch. Then the impossible happened, Spain's transport minister said, as the Renfe train was ordered to proceed in "error". It crashed into the back of the other train between municipalities Mora and Orgaz, about 140km (87 miles) south of Madrid. Some of the passengers were asleep, some had already started their working day on laptops - and others scrolled through their apps on their phones. The journey was interrupted with an announcement that there was congestion on the tracks. This lasted a few minutes - for some, a bit longer for others. items.blurb: The defeated Brazilian candidate claims to be the victim of a coup d’état and political persecution, recycling unsubstantiated allegations of “electoral fraud”.
items.text: Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, who landed in Miami after losing the presidential election on Sunday, has said it was never his intention to "leave my homeland". "I did not flee Brazil; I left for the sake of Brazil," he said in his first statement since his departure. The US provided visas to him and his family after Brazil cancelled his passports as part of a criminal investigation. Bolsonaro denies any wrongdoing. On Wednesday, US President Donald Trump told reporters: "We gave him a pass to come into the country". Newly re-elected President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has criticised Bolsonaro's secretive exit from the country, saying "those who have nothing to hide have nothing to fear". Bolsonaro's arrival in Florida ended days of confusion over his whereabouts, after he was reported to have travelled to Argentina, and then prematurely reported to have already entered the US on Tuesday. items.headline: No clear winner in Israel election with nearly 90 percent of votes counted
items.blurb: Netanyahu's right-wing bloc leads but is falling short of the votes needed to form a government.
items.text: No clear winner has emerged from Israel’s election , with nearly 90 percent of ballots counted and both major political blocs falling short of the 61 seats needed to form a government. The Israeli Central Elections Committee said on Wednesday that it had counted more than five million votes as of 9pm local time (19:00 GMT). Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc is on course to win 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset, while the opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot is expected to secure 48 seats. Projections from Tuesday’s voting also showed that the Arab parties – the Joint List and Ra’am – could hold a record combined 19 seats. Final election results could come as early as Thursday evening, though no clear winner is expected to emerge. More than 500,000 special double-envelope ballots remain to be counted, potentially changing the seat distribution. These include votes cast by soldiers, diplomats and others voting away from their registered polling stations. A year after the fall of El Fasher , the British government said it had sanctioned military leaders from both sides in the country’s ongoing conflict whom it suspected of sexual violence during the siege of the city. A total of 15 commanders from the military groups – the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) – have been subjected to a travel ban and an asset freeze . items.headline: Netanyahu's bloc leading Israel election but short of majority, partial results show
items.blurb: With 85% of ballots counted, Netanyahu's Likud party and its allies are set to win 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset.
items.text: Partial results from Israel's general election show veteran Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is leading his rival, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, but is still short of a majority in parliament. With 85% of ballots counted, Netanyahu's Likud party and its far-right and ultra-Orthodox Jewish allies were on track to win 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset. Eisenkot's Yashar party and three other Jewish opposition parties in his bloc were set for 48. Both leaders have said they will try to form a governing coalition. Arab-led parties, who are on course to win an unprecedented 19 seats, could emerge as kingmakers, but all but one of the Jewish parties have pledged not to work with them. With between 430,000 and 480,000 absentee ballots from groups including soldiers, diplomats and hospital patients yet to be counted, it could still take a day or two for the final election results to emerge. items.headline: New RSS group registers with justice dept to lobby in America
items.blurb: RSS Friends’ Foreign Agents Registration Act (FARA) filing came just days before RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat held a major rally at Madison Square Garden in New York
items.text: A new organisation, RSS Friends registered with the US Department of Justice (DoJ) on August 27 as a foreign agent representing the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), despite the RSS’ previous assertions that it does not lobby in the US. In its filings with the DoJ, RSS Friends explicitly listed the RSS as its “foreign principal” along with the address of the organisation’s new headquarters in Delhi’s Keshav Kunj. The newly registered group also disclosed that its work will remain primarily informational, but that it does not have a written employment or lobbying contract with the RSS with specified compensation and deliverables. RSS spokesperson Sunil Ambekar didn’t respond to queries seeking comment despite multiple reminders. RSS Friends’ Foreign Agents Registration Act (FARA) filing came just days before RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat held a major rally at Madison Square Garden in New York. The RSS, celebrating its centenary this year, is the ideological fount of the Bharatiya Janata Party. “RSS Friends’ proposed activities are primarily informational, educational, public-relations, and community-engagement activities. items.blurb: Elector-to-population ratio released officially by Karnataka CEO shows under-enrolment of about 64.5 lakh electors, of whom roughly 38.41 lakh are in the 18 to 29 age group.
items.text: The 18 to 29 age group accounted for the majority of those missing, calculations showed. File | Photo Credit: Allen Egenuse. J Around 64.5 lakh electors are potentially missing from the final electoral rolls of Karnataka released after the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise on Tuesday (October 27, 2026), based on the Elector-to-Population (E-to-P) ratio of 66.11 released by the office of the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO). The State’s E-to-P ratio quoted in the CEO’s statements was calculated as the ratio between the total number of electors on the rolls and the estimated population in 2026 in all age groups, including those below 18 years of age and not eligible to vote. The 18 to 29 age group accounted for the majority of those missing, calculations further showed. Of the 64.5 lakh potentially missing, 38.41 lakh (59.5%) are in the 18–29 age group. The statements of CEO cited the 2020 Report of the Technical Group on Population Projections, constituted by the National Commission on Population, and widely used by various government agencies, for the population estimates. In the results announced on Wednesday, the BJP’s tally of six was the same as in the 2020 Legislative Council election. The SP had won three seats and independent candidates secured two seats six years ago. The BJP, which was pushed to the back foot in the 2024 Lok Sabha election when its Uttar Pradesh tally fell to 33 from 62 in 2019, was looking to increase its tally in the council election to send the message that it had regained ground before the 2027 assembly election. items.blurb: The Congress fielded sitting MLC Abhijeet Wanjari, who secured 67,231 votes, while the BJP fielded former MLA Sudhakar Kohale, who secured 63,960 votes
items.text: Sitting MLC Abhijeet Wanjari defeated BJP’s Sudhakar Kohale by 3,271 votes. Photo: X/@wanjarri. In a nail-biting contest, Congress candidate and sitting MLC Abhijeet Wanjari defeated his closest rival from the BJP by 3,271 votes to retain the Nagpur Division Graduates’ constituency seat. The counting of votes began on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) morning and concluded in the wee hours of Thursday (October 29, 2026). The Congress had fielded sitting MLC Mr. Wanjari, who secured 67,231 votes. The BJP had fielded former MLA Sudhakar Kohale, who secured 63,960 votes. It is a big setback for the BJP as it has lost in the hometown of Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis and Union Minister Nitin Gadkari who had campaigned extensively for Mr. Kohale. Mr. Kohale was leading his Congress rival by 4,294 votes after the second round of counting on Wednesday (October 28, 2026). After round two of the counting of first-preference votes, Mr. Kohale had polled 60,924 votes while Mr. Wanjari secured 56,630. Independent candidate Nitesh Karale received 24,249 votes. items.headline: Airlines seek more time to shift international flights to Navi Mumbai airport
items.blurb: MIAL presented its redevelopment plans and proposed temporarily shifting international traffic accounting for five million passengers per annum (MPPA) to NMIA.
items.text: Mumbai airport operator Mumbai International Airport Ltd (MIAL) has asked airlines to submit plans by November 3 for temporarily shifting international flights to Navi Mumbai International Airport (NMIA) ahead of the redevelopment of Terminal 1 (T1). Airlines have sought more time, people aware of the development said. "At a meeting with the Airport Airline Operators Committee (AOC) on Wednesday, airlines indicated that the transition should not take place before the winter 2027 schedule, citing the need for advance planning," one person said. "The airlines opposed any unilateral reduction in flight slots from the summer 2027 schedule and called on the airport operator to begin discussions on the winter schedule at the earliest, in line with the civil aviation ministry’s slot-allocation guidelines," they added. The meeting lasted around 90 minutes and was attended by about 50 officials representing 35 airlines. During the meeting, MIAL presented its redevelopment plans and proposed temporarily shifting international traffic accounting for five million passengers per annum (MPPA) to NMIA. items.headline: Lab Rats series: Unlocking the kidney for therapy with Helex
items.blurb: Hyderabad-based Helex Inc is working on a first-in-class mechanism to deliver gene editing drugs safely into the kidneys—a massive medical challenge currently. They not only want to do it first, but also develop it to be affordable for most Indians.
items.text: Mumbai: In 2009, three graduate students shared a flat in London while studying at King’s College. While Poulami Chaudhuri and Anirudh Nishtala pursued master’s degrees in molecular sciences, Rohini Kalvakuntla studied international management. Over a decade later, the three came together to set up a biotech startup in their hometown, Hyderabad, with a clear and ambitious vision—to unlock the kidney cell for therapy and make it affordable for India. Getting the right drug into a kidney cell at the right dose without causing toxicity is a massive medical challenge. Helex Inc. is developing first-in-class genetic medicines to target the kidney. “The motivation was to have top-class medicine and science, but it has to be accessible and affordable for patients in India and worldwide,” said Kalvakuntla, who is chief business officer at Helex. The idea stems from a large number of innovative therapies—especially for genetic, rare and critical illnesses—remaining unaffordable to the majority of the domestic population, even when launched in India. The firm’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 1,823 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,176 crore in FY25, according to its audited financial statements. Astrotalk operates a digital astrology platform that connects users with astrologers for paid consultations via chat, calls and video. Revenue from consultations rose 45% to Rs 1,657 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,139 crore in FY25, and accounted for around 91% of operating revenue. International revenue surged 2.6 times to Rs 621 crore from Rs 236 crore, with its share of total revenue at 34% against 20% a year earlier. items.blurb: Across a business, any number of AI platforms, systems, and tools may be at work simultaneously—for example, AI-powered customer platforms, conversational assistants, and workflow and process automation tools. Each one is sophisticated, advanced, and quick to respond.
items.text: Across a business, any number of AI platforms, systems, and tools may be at work simultaneously—for example, AI-powered customer platforms, conversational assistants, and workflow and process automation tools. Each one is sophisticated, advanced, and quick to respond. But, when set to work, the outcomes and actions that emerge may be wrong, confused, or lacking a proper understanding of the business. Many organizations find themselves in this situation—and it could be one of key reasons they struggle to extract returns on their AI investments. An MIT Technology Review Insights poll finds that while every organization surveyed is using AI today to some degree, fewer than one in five (16%) are extracting transformative value from their deployments. The largest percentage of respondents (40%) say they are seeing moderate gains in specific tasks or teams, while 21% report meaningful gains, leaving 23% that are seeing minimal returns or none at all. items.headline: Pairing industrial AI autonomy and human control
items.text: Living digital twins are helping industrial plants run more like living systems, and setting the stage for industries that work in sync. Most people associate industrial environments with cold steel and clockwork machinery. Functionally, though, a plant or factory is more like a living thing: It has a pulse, even a metabolism. It goes through wear and tear as it ages, and signs of deteriorating health often show up as barely perceptible irregularities. Digital twin technology has long aimed to mirror that dynamism and model anomalies that may be symptomatic of larger problems. But earlier implementations were a few beats behind physical reality; they were incapable of real-time analysis and unable to proactively address any issues detected. They focused more on simulation, observation and what-if scenario planning, rather than closed-loop execution. Rather than serving as a digital mirror of reality that can spot anomalies or suggest optimizations, a living digital twin combines a dynamic, high-fidelity digital representation of complex operations with the capacity to intervene in the physical world through operations and control systems. items.headline: The focus on AI safety disasters ignores everyday harms
items.blurb: Consider what passes for success in technology policy. An AI company promises that its chatbot will not encourage suicide. A social media platform makes it more difficult for children to buy fentanyl. These are important protections, and they should have existed all along.
items.text: Consider what passes for success in technology policy. An AI company promises that its chatbot will not encourage suicide . A social media platform makes it more difficult for children to buy fentanyl . These are important protections, and they should have existed all along. But companies can clear these low bars while continuing to make products that leave young people dependent on simulated friendships or trapped in feeds built to keep them scrolling. We have historically allowed the debate over technology to be defined by the worst thing a product might do, with remarkably little discussion of the insidious damage it does every day. As we transition into an era defined by powerful AI products, we should demand that the tech industry do more than merely address catastrophic harms. We should take measures to ensure that its products don’t erode how we think, learn, and interact with one another.
